stem.text: Let f be a continuous function with \( \int_{-4}^{2} f(x)\,dx = 9 \) and \( \int_{-1}^{2} f(x)\,dx = -3 \). Find the value of \( \int_{-1}^{-4} \left(-f(x) + 2\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Reverse the requested integral and use linearity: \( \int_{-1}^{-4} \left(-f(x) + 2\right) dx = -(-1) \int_{-4}^{-1} f(x)\,dx + (2)(-4 - -1) \), and the constant contributes \( -6 \).

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, the requested integral runs right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: constant multiple plus a constant term

distractor_derivations.A: sign change for the reversed target integral left out
distractor_derivations.C: split written with its limits reversed, taking the integral from -4 to -1 as -3 - (9)
distractor_derivations.D: constant term integrated as if its limits ran left to right, so its sign change is left out
